target_customer: Consumers who want a private automatic journal of their life
problem: People forget their daily moments and have no easy private place that gathers and resurfaces them over time.
business_model: Consumer app, planned paid tier and printed books of memories

founders.name: Yu-Kuan Lin
founders.background_notes: YC page lists current role as SVP and Head of Product at Diligent; no earlier background given

founders.name: Weiting Liu
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page only; the 2013 BNext profile names two co-founders

competitors.name: Day One
competitors.what: iOS journal app with timeline, calendar and geotagging, text focused

competitors.name: Momento
competitors.what: iOS journal with tags for people and places, imports from many services

competitors.name: Diaro
competitors.what: Android journal with web interface and Dropbox sync

competitors.name: Memoire
competitors.what: Android journal with mood, weather and audio attachments

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile journal with timeline, daily resurfacing emails and social import was standard app engineering for a two person team in 2012.

defensibility.rationale: Several journal apps already offered similar timelines and imports, and a TNW review in December 2012 noted no export and no sharing, so little locked users in beyond the data they entered.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied it that the sources show; the company went inactive with no public cause.

market_need_then: Demand for personal journaling and life logging existed in 2012, shown by several competing apps; BNext reported about 20,000 users by early 2013 for the free iPhone app.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence about the brand itself was found; the name is descriptive and generic.

outcome_analysis: Everyday.me launched an automatic journal in August 2012 into a field with Day One, Momento and others. It reached about 20,000 users by early 2013 and planned paid tiers, but no funding, acquisition or shutdown account was found, so the cause of its inactive status is not public and the failure code other is a placeholder.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 522 on fetch. Funding databases list an unrelated company named Everyme (Tencent, Andreessen, Greylock round of 2.15M USD, Sept 2012); no source ties it to Everyday.me, so none of it is recorded. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition story. Founder education and prior employers not found. Competitor Path appears in the TNW review only as a comparison and is not listed.
